title: The sheaf of modules on Proj(S) attached to a graded module exists
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be an $\mathbf N$-graded commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj] with its standard opens $D_+(f)$ and $\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O_X)=S_{(f)}$ for $f$ homogeneous of positive degree [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and let $M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n$ be a graded $S$-module. For such $f$ let $M_{(f)}$ be the degree-zero part of $M_f=M\otimes_SS_f$, i.e. the $S_{(f)}$-module of fractions $x/f^m$ with $m\ge0$ and $x\in M_{m\deg f}$. Then: (a) if $g$ is homogeneous of positive degree with $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$, then $g^e=af$ for some $e\ge1$ and homogeneous $a\in S$, and $x/f^m\mapsto a^mx/g^{em}$ is a well-defined $S_{(f)}$-linear map $\rho_{f,g}:M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$, independent of the choice of $e,a$, with $\rho_{f,f}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{g,h}\rho_{f,g}=\rho_{f,h}$, and an isomorphism when $D_+(f)=D_+(g)$; (b) there is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F(D_+(f))=M_{(f)}$ as $S_{(f)}$-modules for every homogeneous $f$ of positive degree and with restriction maps $\rho_{f,g}$, and it is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with these identifications; (c) $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and its stalk at the point $x$ given by the homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$ is $M_{(\mathfrak p)}$ (fractions $y/h$, $h\notin\mathfrak p$ homogeneous, $\deg y=\deg h$); (d) for every $m\in M_0$ the elements $m/1\in M_{(f)}$ are compatible under the $\rho_{f,g}$ and are the restrictions of a unique global section of $\mathcal F$; this gives an $S_0$-linear map $M_0\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$.

proof.text: *Standard opens.* By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion]: the standard opens $D_+(f)$ ($f$ homogeneous of positive degree) form a basis $\mathcal B$ of the topology of $X$ with $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$ (clause (0)); in particular they cover $X$. $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ iff $g^e=af$ for some $e\ge1$ and homogeneous $a$ (clause (1)); every open covering of a standard open is refined by a finite covering by standard opens (clause (2)); and $D_+(f)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^nD_+(g_i)$ iff the $g_i^{\deg f}/f^{\deg g_i}$ generate the unit ideal of $S_{(f)}$ (clause (3)).

*Clause (a).* Let $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$. By step 1, $g^e=af$ with $e\ge1$ and $a$ homogeneous. By [lem-weil-pbc-graded-module-away-restriction] (i), $x/f^m\mapsto a^mx/g^{em}$ is a well-defined map $\rho_{f,g}:M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$, equal to the restriction of the unique $S$-linear map $M_f\to M_g$ with $x/1\mapsto x/1$, hence independent of $(e,a)$, and semilinear over the ring map $\rho^S_{f,g}:S_{(f)}\to S_{(g)}$, i.e. $S_{(f)}$-linear for the $S_{(f)}$-module structure of $M_{(g)}$ through $\rho^S_{f,g}$. By (ii) of that lemma, $\rho_{f,f}=\mathrm{id}$ (take $e=1$, $a=1$) and $\rho_{g,h}\rho_{f,g}=\rho_{f,h}$ when $D_+(h)\subseteq D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ (step 1 gives the relations $h^{e'}=a'g$, $g^e=af$). If $D_+(f)=D_+(g)$, both $\rho_{f,g}$ and $\rho_{g,f}$ are defined and $\rho_{g,f}\rho_{f,g}=\rho_{f,f}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{f,g}\rho_{g,f}=\rho_{g,g}=\mathrm{id}$, so $\rho_{f,g}$ is an isomorphism (for $M=S$ a ring isomorphism). This is (a).

By step 2 these satisfy $r_{U,U}=\mathrm{id}$, $r_{V,W}r_{U,V}=r_{U,W}$, $r_{U,V}(bs)=r^S_{U,V}(b)\,r_{U,V}(s)$, and for any other $f$ with $D_+(f)=U$ the isomorphisms $ho_{f_U,f}$ identify $(M_{(f_U)},r)$ with $(M_{(f)},ho)$ compatibly (by transitivity). proof.text: *Sheaf condition on finite standard coverings.* Let $U=D_+(f)=\bigcup_{i=1}^nD_+(g_i)$ with $g_i$ homogeneous of positive degree. Since $D_+(g_i)\subseteq D_+(f)$, $D_+(g_i)=D_+(fg_i)$ and $D_+(g_i)\cap D_+(g_j)=D_+(fg_ig_j)$ (step 1), so via the isomorphisms of step 2 the sheaf sequence for this covering is $0\to M_{(f)}\to\bigoplus_iM_{(fg_i)}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{(fg_ig_j)}$ with the maps $\rho$ (differences in the last arrow). Put $u_i=g_i^{\deg f}/f^{\deg g_i}\in S_{(f)}$. By step 1 (clause (3)) the $u_i$ generate the unit ideal of $S_{(f)}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-graded-module-away-restriction] (iii) to the pairs $(f,fg_i)$ (relation $(fg_i)^1=g_i\cdot f$) and $(f,fg_ig_j)$ (relation $(fg_ig_j)^1=(g_ig_j)f$): the corresponding elements are $(fg_i)^{\deg f}/f^{\deg f+\deg g_i}=u_i$ and $(fg_ig_j)^{\deg f}/f^{\deg f+\deg g_i+\deg g_j}=u_iu_j$, so $\theta$ gives isomorphisms $(M_{(f)})_{u_i}\cong M_{(fg_i)}$ and $(M_{(f)})_{u_iu_j}\cong M_{(fg_ig_j)}$, and by (iv) of that lemma (with $h=fg_ig_j$, $g=fg_i$, resp. $g=fg_j$; and with $g=f$, where $\theta_{f,f}$ is the identity of $(M_{(f)})_1=M_{(f)}$) they carry the maps $\rho_{f,fg_i}$ and $\rho_{fg_i,fg_ig_j}$, $\rho_{fg_j,fg_ig_j}$ to the canonical localization maps $M_{(f)}\to(M_{(f)})_{u_i}\to(M_{(f)})_{u_iu_j}$ and $(M_{(f)})_{u_j}\to(M_{(f)})_{u_iu_j}$. Hence the sheaf sequence is isomorphic to $0\to M'\to\bigoplus_iM'_{u_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M'_{u_iu_j}$ for the $S_{(f)}$-module $M'=M_{(f)}$, which is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] applied to $R=S_{(f)}$, $u_1,\dots,u_n$. So $F$ satisfies the sheaf condition for every finite covering of a member of $\mathcal B$ by members of $\mathcal B$.

proof.text: *Clause (b).* By step 1, $\mathcal B$ is a basis closed under pairwise intersections ($D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$), and every covering of a member of $\mathcal B$ by members of $\mathcal B$ is refined by a finite one. With the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_X$ and the presheaf of modules $F$ of step 3, which satisfies the finite sheaf condition by step 4, [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-of-modules-from-basis] (a) gives a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F=F^{ext}$ with $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear isomorphisms $\mathcal F(U)\cong F(U)=M_{(f_U)}$ compatible with the restrictions; composing with the isomorphisms $\rho_{f_U,f}$ of step 2 gives $\mathcal F(D_+(f))\cong M_{(f)}$ for every homogeneous $f$ of positive degree, as $S_{(f)}\cong\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O_X)$-modules (step 3), with restriction maps $\rho_{f,g}$ (transitivity, step 2). Uniqueness: if $\mathcal G$ is another sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $S_{(f)}$-linear identifications $\mathcal G(D_+(f))\cong M_{(f)}$ compatible with the $\rho$, the composites $F(U)\cong\mathcal G(U)$ are $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear, bijective and compatible with restrictions, so by clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-of-modules-from-basis] there is a unique morphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ inducing them, and it is an isomorphism; any isomorphism compatible with the identifications induces these maps on $\mathcal B$, so it is this one. This is (b) (Stacks Definition 01M6 (3), Lemma 01M7 (2),(3)).

proof.text: *Clause (c), quasi-coherence.* Fix $f$ homogeneous of degree $d>0$ and let $\iota_f:\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}\to X$ be the open immersion with image $D_+(f)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], an isomorphism of schemes $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}\cong D_+(f)$ inducing $\theta_f$ on global sections. Let $D(r)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ be a principal open. Write $r=h/f^n$ with $h\in S_{nd}$; replacing $(h,n)$ by $(hf,n+1)$ we may assume $n\ge1$, so $h$ is homogeneous of positive degree $nd$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] (with $g=h$, $e=nd$), $\iota_f^{-1}(D_+(h))=D(h^d/f^{nd})=D(r^d)=D(r)$, i.e. $\iota_f(D(r))=D_+(f)\cap D_+(h)=D_+(fh)$ (Stacks Lemma 01MA). For the pair $(f,fh)$ (relation $(fh)^1=h\cdot f$) the element of [lem-weil-pbc-graded-module-away-restriction] (iii) is $(fh)^d/f^{d+nd}=h^d/f^{nd}=r^d$, so $\mathcal F(D_+(fh))\cong M_{(fh)}\cong(M_{(f)})_{r^d}=(M_{(f)})_r$, and for $M=S$, $\Gamma(D_+(fh),\mathcal O_X)\cong S_{(fh)}\cong(S_{(f)})_r=\Gamma(D(r),\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}})$. The latter composite agrees with the isomorphism induced by $\iota_f$: both are $S_{(f)}$-algebra maps $\Gamma(D_+(fh),\mathcal O_X)\to(S_{(f)})_r$ (compatible with restriction from $D_+(f)$, resp. from $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$, and $\theta_f$), and $\Gamma(D_+(fh),\mathcal O_X)\cong(S_{(f)})_r$ is a localization of $S_{(f)}$ at $r$, out of which an $S_{(f)}$-algebra map is unique. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (with $R=S_{(f)}$, $N=M_{(f)}$), $\widetilde{M_{(f)}}(D(r))=(M_{(f)})_r$ as $(S_{(f)})_r$-modules with the canonical localization maps as restrictions; by (iv) of [lem-weil-pbc-graded-module-away-restriction] the isomorphisms $\mathcal F(D_+(fh))\cong(M_{(f)})_r$ carry the restrictions $\rho$ to these localization maps. The principal opens of $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ form a basis closed under intersection ($D(r)\cap D(r')=D(rr')$) and coverings of a $D(r)$ by principal opens refine to finite ones ($D(r)$ is quasi-compact), so by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-of-modules-from-basis] (b), on the space $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ with the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}}$, the family of these isomorphisms extends to an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}}$-modules $\iota_f^*(\mathcal F|_{D_+(f)})\cong\widetilde{M_{(f)}}$. So $\mathcal F|_{D_+(f)}$ is isomorphic, via the affine scheme $D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$, to the sheaf associated to the $S_{(f)}$-module $M_{(f)}$; since the $D_+(f)$ cover $X$ (step 1), $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent].

*Clause (c), stalks.* Let $x\in X$ with homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$, and let $T$ be the set of homogeneous elements of $S$ not in $\mathfrak p$; $M_{(\mathfrak p)}$ is the set of $y/t$ in $T^{-1}M$ with $t\in T$, $y\in M$ homogeneous, $\deg y=\deg t$, and $y/t=0$ iff $cy=0$ for some $c\in T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-of-modules-from-basis] (c) and step 5, $\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is the colimit of $M_{(f)}$ over the homogeneous $f
otin\mathfrak p$ of positive degree, preordered by $f\ge f'$ iff $D_+(f)\subseteq D_+(f')$, with transition maps $ho$ (directed: $ff'\ge f,f'$). The maps $\mu_f:M_{(f)}	o M_{(\mathfrak p)}$, $x/f^m\mapsto x/f^m$, are compatible: $\mu_g(ho_{f,g}(x/f^m))=a^mx/g^{em}=x/f^m$ since $a^mf^m=g^{em}$ and $f,g\in T$. So they induce $\mu:\mathcal F_x	o M_{(\mathfrak p)}$. Surjective: since $S_+

otin\mathfrak p$ homogeneous of positive degree; for $y/t\in M_{(\mathfrak p)}$ put $f=tf_0$ (homogeneous of positive degree, $
otin\mathfrak p$); then $y/t=yf_0/f$ with $\deg(yf_0)=\deg f$, i.e. $y/t=\mu_f(yf_0/f^1)$. Injective: if $\mu_f(x/f^m)=0$, there is $c\in T$ with $cx=0$; then $fc$ is homogeneous of positive degree, $

proof.text: *Clause (d).* Let $m\in M_0$. For every $f$, $m/1=m/f^0\in M_{(f)}$ (degree $0=0\cdot\deg f$). If $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$, $g^e=af$, then $\rho_{f,g}(m/f^0)=a^0m/g^0=m/1$ (step 2). The standard opens cover $X$ and $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$ (step 1), and under the identifications of step 5 both $m/1\in\mathcal F(D_+(f))$ and $m/1\in\mathcal F(D_+(g))$ restrict to $m/1\in\mathcal F(D_+(fg))$. By the sheaf property of $\mathcal F$ there is a unique $s_m\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ with $s_m|_{D_+(f)}=m/1$ for all $f$ (uniqueness: two such sections agree on a covering). The map $m\mapsto s_m$ is additive ($(m+m')/1=m/1+m'/1$ and uniqueness). For $r\in S_0$, the same construction for $M=S$ gives the global function $s_r\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ with $s_r|_{D_+(f)}=\theta_f(r/1)$ (step 3), and $r\mapsto s_r$ is a ring map $S_0\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$; since $(rm)/1=(r/1)(m/1)$ in $M_{(f)}$, $s_rs_m$ and $s_{rm}$ have the same restriction to every $D_+(f)$, so $s_{rm}=s_rs_m$. Hence $M_0\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$, $m\mapsto s_m$, is $S_0$-linear. This is (d) (Stacks Lemma 01M7 (6)).
